newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawyers oppose curbs on civil rights.
newsitem.headline: HK lawyers oppose curbs on civil rights.

text.p: Hong Kong lawyers on Friday added their voice to opposition to plans to curb civil and political liberties after the British colony is handed back to China in July.

"The Bar Council maintains its view that the Societies Ordinance and the Public Order Ordinance do not contravene any provision of the Basic Law," the Bar Association said in an analysis paper submitted to Tung's office.

China's National People's Congress (NPC), or parliament, in February declared parts of Hong Kong's Public Order and Societies ordinances incompatible with the Basic Law, the territory's future constitution promulgated by Beijing, and resolved to change a string of laws protecting civil liberties and rights.
The changes will take effect on July 1, when the territory returns to China after 150 years of British rule.
Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa followed this month with plans to curb political freedoms after the handover and launched what he called a "public consultation" on the proposals.
He also proposed a ban on foreign donations to local political groups and restrictions on the right to protest.
As part of the consultation, various interest groups have been submitting written comments on the plan.
The Bar Association criticised the three-week-long consultation, which will end on Wednesday, saying it had been arranged too hastily and more time was needed.
"We do not perceive any great danger to the (future) government if the laws governing these matters are not in place at the time of the changeover," it said.
On Thursday, Hong Kong business lobbies backed the plan, saying Tung's proposals were no more restrictive than laws in force in the United States, Canada and Australia.
Pro-democracy groups fiercely oppose Tung's plans.
